test_1_cluster_creation.name: test_1_cluster_creation
test_1_cluster_creation.title: Create Test HCP Cluster
test_1_cluster_creation.objective: Create a ROSA HCP cluster in the srep-dev sector that will serve as the foundation for metrics, logs, and synthetic monitoring tests
test_1_cluster_creation.intention: This test validates that the test infrastructure can be provisioned correctly. The cluster creation process includes automatic configuration of remote write for metrics and log forwarding to RHOBS. Without a successfully created cluster, no observability data flows can be tested.
test_1_cluster_creation.why_it_matters: Cluster creation is the foundation for all RHOBS testing. It validates that the test sector (srep-dev) has capacity, that the fleet-manager can provision HCP clusters, and that the cluster is properly configured for observability data forwarding. This test also creates the HostedCluster CR on the Management Cluster which triggers the synthetic monitoring probe registration.

steps.title: Generate Unique Cluster Name
steps.command:
export TEST_CLUSTER_NAME="metrics-test-$(date +%s)"
echo "Creating cluster: $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME"
steps.description: Creates a unique timestamp-based cluster name to avoid conflicts
steps.expected_result: Cluster name variable set with timestamp suffix

steps.title: Create ROSA HCP Cluster in srep-dev Sector
steps.command:
rosa create cluster \
  --cluster-name=$TEST_CLUSTER_NAME \
  --sts \
  --mode=auto \
  --hosted-cp \
  --properties=provision-shard-id:srep-dev \
  --region=$TEST_REGION \
  --yes
steps.description: Creates a ROSA HCP cluster targeting the srep-dev sector (dedicated E2E test environment)
steps.expected_result: Command succeeds and cluster creation begins
steps.expected_output:
I: Creating cluster '<cluster-name>'
I: To view a list of clusters and their status, run 'rosa list clusters'

steps.title: Wait for Cluster to be Ready
steps.command: rosa logs install --cluster $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME -f
steps.description: Monitors cluster creation progress by following installation logs. Cluster takes 10-15 minutes to reach 'ready' state.
steps.expected_result: Cluster reaches 'ready' state
alternative_commands: while true; do STATE=$(rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME -o json | jq -r '.state'); echo "Cluster state: $STATE"; if [ "$STATE" = "ready" ]; then echo "Cluster is ready!"; break; fi; sleep 30; done

steps.title: Capture Cluster Details
steps.command:
export CLUSTER_ID=$(rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME -o json | jq -r '.id')
export CLUSTER_API_URL=$(rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME -o json | jq -r '.api.url')

echo "Cluster ID: $CLUSTER_ID"
echo "API URL: $CLUSTER_API_URL"

cat > /tmp/test-cluster-details.txt <<EOF
Test Cluster Details
--------------------
Name: $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
ID: $CLUSTER_ID
API URL: $CLUSTER_API_URL
Created: $(date)
EOF
steps.description: Extracts and saves cluster metadata (ID and API URL) needed for subsequent tests
steps.expected_result: Cluster ID and API URL captured and saved to file

success_indicators: Cluster created successfully in srep-dev sector
Cluster ID and API URL obtained
HostedCluster CR created on Management Cluster
expected_results.what_success_means: The test infrastructure is provisioned and ready for observability testing. The cluster's metrics and logs are automatically configured to forward to RHOBS. The HostedCluster CR on the MC will trigger synthetic monitoring probe creation.
expected_results.what_failure_means: Infrastructure provisioning is blocked. This could indicate sector capacity issues, fleet-manager problems, or AWS service issues. No subsequent tests can proceed without a working cluster.

failure_scenarios.likely_cause: Management cluster at quota or sector capacity exhausted
debugging_steps: Check sector capacity: ocm list provision-shards | grep $TEST_SECTOR
List existing clusters in sector to identify cleanup candidates
failure_scenarios.remediation: Contact fleet-manager team to increase quota or clean up old clusters
failure_scenarios.automation_gap: No automated capacity checks before cluster creation

failure_scenarios.likely_cause: Typo in sector name or sector doesn't exist
debugging_steps: Verify sector name: ocm list provision-shards
failure_scenarios.remediation: Correct sector name in TEST_SECTOR environment variable
failure_scenarios.automation_gap: Should validate sector exists before attempting creation

failure_scenarios.likely_cause: AWS service issues or control plane provisioning failure
debugging_steps: Check installation logs: rosa logs install -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
Check cluster status: rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
failure_scenarios.remediation: Review logs for specific errors, may need to delete and recreate cluster
failure_scenarios.automation_gap: No timeout handling or automatic retry logic

pass_criteria: HCP cluster created in srep-dev sector

automation.automation_notes: This test should be automated as part of E2E suite setup/teardown. Consider using existing cluster pool instead of creating new cluster each time.

debugging_checklist: Verify AWS account credentials are valid

test_1_cluster_creation.educational_notes: ROSA HCP (Hosted Control Plane) clusters have their control plane hosted on a Management Cluster, while worker nodes run in the customer's AWS account. The srep-dev sector is a dedicated test environment maintained by the SRE team. When a cluster is created, OCM automatically configures metrics remote-write to RHOBS and creates a HostedCluster CR on the MC.

test_2_logs_flow.name: test_2_logs_flow
test_2_logs_flow.title: Logs Flow End-to-End
test_2_logs_flow.objective: Verify that logs (application and API audit logs) from an HCP cluster flow to Loki and are queryable in Grafana
test_2_logs_flow.intention: This test validates the complete log forwarding pipeline from HCP clusters to Loki. It ensures that both application logs and API audit logs are captured, forwarded, labeled correctly, and queryable.
test_2_logs_flow.why_it_matters: Log forwarding is critical for troubleshooting customer clusters and detecting security issues. Application logs help debug workload problems, while API audit logs track all API operations for security and compliance. If log forwarding fails, SREs lose visibility into cluster and workload behavior.
prerequisites: Newly created HCP cluster from Test 1
CLUSTER_ID and CLUSTER_API_URL environment variables set

steps.title: Create Unique Log Marker
steps.command:
export LOG_MARKER="e2e-test-$(date +%s)-$(uuidgen | cut -d- -f1)"
echo "Log marker: $LOG_MARKER"
steps.description: Generates a unique identifier to tag test logs for easy searching in Loki
steps.expected_result: LOG_MARKER variable set with timestamp and UUID

steps.title: Deploy Log-Generating Pod
steps.command:
cat <<EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: log-generator
  namespace: metrics-test
  labels:
    app: log-generator
spec:
  containers:
  - name: logger
    image: busybox:latest
    command:
    - /bin/sh
    - -c
    - |
      while true; do
        echo "INFO: $LOG_MARKER - Test log entry \$(date)"
        echo "WARN: $LOG_MARKER - Warning message \$(date)"
        echo "ERROR: $LOG_MARKER - Error message \$(date)"
        sleep 10
      done
  restartPolicy: Always
EOF
steps.description: Deploys a pod that continuously generates logs at INFO, WARN, and ERROR levels with the unique marker
steps.expected_result: Pod created in metrics-test namespace

steps.title: Verify Pod is Running and Generating Logs
steps.command:
oc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/log-generator -n metrics-test --timeout=60s
oc logs -n metrics-test log-generator --tail=10
steps.description: Confirms pod is running and logs contain the unique marker
steps.expected_result: Pod shows Ready status and logs display with LOG_MARKER present

steps.title: Trigger API Operations
steps.command:
oc create namespace audit-test-$(date +%s)
oc get nodes
oc get pods -A --limit=10
oc delete namespace audit-test-*
steps.description: Performs various API operations (create, read, delete) to generate audit log entries
steps.expected_result: API operations succeed and generate audit logs

steps.title: Verify Audit Logging is Enabled
steps.command: rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME | grep -i audit
steps.description: Confirms that audit logging is enabled for the HCP cluster (automatic in HCP)
steps.expected_result: Audit logging configuration visible in cluster description

steps.title: Wait for Log Propagation
steps.command:
echo "Waiting 5 minutes for logs to propagate to Loki..."
sleep 300
steps.description: Allows time for logs to be forwarded from cluster to Loki (typically 2-5 minutes)
steps.expected_result: 5 minute wait completes

steps.title: Query Application Logs
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOKI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query={cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\",namespace=\"metrics-test\"} |= \"$LOG_MARKER\"" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=100" \
  "$LOKI_API_URL/loki/api/v1/query_range" | jq
steps.description: Queries Loki for application logs with our unique marker
steps.expected_result: Returns log entries from log-generator pod with correct labels and content

steps.title: Verify Log Labels
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOKI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query={cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"} |= \"$LOG_MARKER\"" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=1" \
  "$LOKI_API_URL/loki/api/v1/query_range" | \
  jq '.data.result[0].stream'
steps.description: Extracts and verifies log labels include cluster_id, namespace, pod, container
steps.expected_result: Log stream labels contain all required metadata

steps.title: Query API Audit Logs
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOKI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query={cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\",log_type=\"audit\"}" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10" \
  "$LOKI_API_URL/loki/api/v1/query_range" | jq

curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOKI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query={cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\",log_type=\"audit\"} |~ \"create.*namespace\"" \
  "$LOKI_API_URL/loki/api/v1/query_range" | jq '.data.result | length'
steps.description: Queries for API audit logs from our test operations
steps.expected_result: Finds audit log entries for namespace creation and other API operations

steps.title: Query Logs via Grafana
steps.description: Verifies logs are queryable through Grafana UI or API
steps.expected_result: Logs display in Grafana with timestamps and filtering capabilities

steps.title: Check Log Continuity
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOKI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query=count_over_time({cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\",namespace=\"metrics-test\"} |= \"$LOG_MARKER\" [30m])" \
  "$LOKI_API_URL/loki/api/v1/query" | jq
steps.description: Counts log entries over 30 minutes to verify continuous log stream (expects ~540 logs: 3 logs/10 sec * 6/min * 30 min)
steps.expected_result: Continuous log stream with no gaps, approximately 540 entries

success_indicators: Application logs appear in Loki within 10 minutes
API audit logs appear in Loki
Logs include correct labels (cluster_id, namespace, pod, container)
Logs queryable via Grafana with LogQL
Continuous log stream with no gaps
expected_results.what_success_means: The log forwarding pipeline is fully operational. Application logs from workloads and audit logs from the API server are both captured, labeled correctly, and stored in Loki. SREs can query logs for troubleshooting and security analysis.
expected_results.what_failure_means: Log forwarding is broken or misconfigured. This creates a blind spot for troubleshooting workload issues and detecting security events. Missing logs can delay incident resolution and violate compliance requirements.

failure_scenarios.symptom: No logs found in Loki after 10 minutes
failure_scenarios.likely_cause: Log forwarding not configured or fluentd/vector pods not running
debugging_steps: Check ClusterLogging CR exists: oc get clusterlogging -A
Check logging operator status: oc get pods -n openshift-logging
Check forwarder configuration: oc get clusterlogforwarder -A -o yaml
Check fluentd/vector logs for errors: oc logs -n openshift-logging <pod>
failure_scenarios.remediation: Verify log forwarding configuration in app-interface, ensure Loki endpoint is reachable
failure_scenarios.automation_gap: Should automatically verify log forwarding configuration on cluster creation

failure_scenarios.symptom: Application logs present but missing labels
failure_scenarios.likely_cause: Label configuration issue in log forwarding pipeline
debugging_steps: Review ClusterLogForwarder configuration for label mappings
Check for errors in fluentd/vector processing pipeline
failure_scenarios.remediation: Update log forwarding pipeline configuration to include required labels

failure_scenarios.likely_cause: Audit log forwarding disabled for HCP clusters
debugging_steps: Verify HCP audit log forwarding is enabled in stage environment
Check if audit policy is configured: rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
failure_scenarios.remediation: Consult with team about HCP audit log configuration requirements
failure_scenarios.automation_gap: Should verify audit logging is enabled before attempting to query

failure_scenarios.likely_cause: Log forwarding failures or Loki ingestion issues
debugging_steps: Check fluentd/vector metrics for dropped logs
Check Loki distributor logs for errors
Verify network connectivity between cluster and Loki
failure_scenarios.remediation: Investigate and resolve log forwarding or Loki ingestion issues
failure_scenarios.automation_gap: Should monitor for gaps in log continuity

pass_criteria: Application logs appear in Loki within 10 minutes
API audit logs appear in Loki
Logs include correct labels (cluster_id, namespace, pod)
Logs queryable via Grafana with LogQL
Continuous log stream with no gaps

automation.automation_notes: Should be automated to run continuously. Consider using existing log markers to avoid creating test workloads. May need to mock audit log generation.

sop_references.description: Placeholder for SOP on debugging log forwarding issues

debugging_checklist: Verify ClusterLogging and ClusterLogForwarder CRs exist
Check openshift-logging namespace pods are running
Verify Loki endpoint is reachable from cluster

test_2_logs_flow.educational_notes: HCP clusters forward logs using the OpenShift cluster-logging-operator and either fluentd or vector as the collection agent. Logs are labeled with cluster_id, namespace, pod, and container metadata before being sent to Loki. Loki stores logs as streams (groups of log entries with identical labels) and allows querying using LogQL, a query language similar to PromQL. API audit logs track all requests to the Kubernetes API server and are essential for security and compliance.

test_3_synthetic_monitoring.name: test_3_synthetic_monitoring
test_3_synthetic_monitoring.title: Synthetic Monitoring Flow End-to-End
test_3_synthetic_monitoring.objective: Verify the complete synthetic monitoring flow: RMO detects HCP cluster → registers probe in API → agent picks up probe → blackbox executes probe → metrics appear in RHOBS
test_3_synthetic_monitoring.intention: This test validates the entire synthetic monitoring system that continuously probes cluster API endpoints for availability. It ensures all components work together: route-monitor-operator (RMO), rhobs-synthetics-api, rhobs-synthetics-agent, blackbox-exporter, and the metrics pipeline to RHOBS.
test_3_synthetic_monitoring.why_it_matters: Synthetic monitoring provides external validation that cluster APIs are reachable and responsive. It's the first line of defense for detecting cluster availability issues, often before customers report problems. This test ensures the synthetic monitoring system can automatically discover new clusters, configure probes, execute them, and report results to RHOBS where they power customer-facing dashboards and SRE alerts.
prerequisites: HCP cluster from Test 1 (or create new one)
CLUSTER_ID and CLUSTER_API_URL environment variables set

steps.title: Login to Management Cluster
steps.command:
export MC_CLUSTER_ID="<mc-cluster-id>"  # From setup
ocm backplane login $MC_CLUSTER_ID
oc whoami
steps.description: Connects to the Management Cluster where route-monitor-operator runs and HostedCluster CRs exist
steps.expected_result: Successfully authenticated to MC, oc whoami shows username

steps.title: Check RMO Deployment
steps.command:
export RMO_NS=$(oc get deployment -A | grep route-monitor-operator | awk '{print $1}')
echo "RMO Namespace: $RMO_NS"
oc get deployment -n $RMO_NS route-monitor-operator -o yaml
oc get deployment -n $RMO_NS route-monitor-operator -o yaml | grep -A3 "probe-api-url"
steps.description: Verifies RMO is deployed and configured with the correct RHOBS synthetics API endpoint
steps.expected_result: RMO deployment exists and probe-api-url points to RHOBS synthetics API

steps.title: Check RMO Logs
steps.command: oc logs -n $RMO_NS deployment/route-monitor-operator --tail=50
steps.description: Reviews recent RMO logs for errors or connection issues
steps.expected_result: No errors in logs, successful API connections visible

steps.title: Check HostedCluster CR Exists
steps.command:
oc get hostedclusters -A
oc get hostedclusters -A | grep $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
export HC_NAMESPACE=$(oc get hostedclusters -A | grep $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME | awk '{print $1}')
oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NAMESPACE $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME -o yaml
steps.description: Locates the HostedCluster CR for our test cluster that RMO watches
steps.expected_result: HostedCluster CR exists with correct metadata and API endpoint

steps.title: Verify API URL in HostedCluster
steps.description: Extracts the API URL from HostedCluster status and compares to expected value
steps.expected_result: API URLs match (HC_API_URL is the host portion of CLUSTER_API_URL)

steps.title: Monitor RMO Watching HostedCluster
steps.command: oc logs -n $RMO_NS deployment/route-monitor-operator -f | grep -i "hostedcluster\|$TEST_CLUSTER_NAME"
steps.description: Watches RMO logs for evidence it detected the HostedCluster
steps.expected_result: Log entries showing HostedCluster detection, e.g. 'Detected new HostedCluster: <cluster-name>'

steps.title: Wait for Probe Registration
steps.command:
echo "Waiting 2 minutes for probe registration..."
sleep 120
steps.description: Allows time for RMO to register probe with RHOBS API (typically 1-2 minutes)
steps.expected_result: 2 minute wait completes

steps.title: Query RHOBS API for Probe
steps.command:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/probes" | \
  jq '.probes[] | select(.labels.cluster_id == "'"$CLUSTER_ID"'")'
steps.description: Queries RHOBS synthetics API for the probe registered for our cluster
steps.expected_result: Returns probe object with cluster_id label matching our cluster

steps.title: Capture Probe ID
steps.command:
export PROBE_ID=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/probes" | \
  jq -r '.probes[] | select(.labels.cluster_id == "'"$CLUSTER_ID"'") | .id')

echo "Probe ID: $PROBE_ID"

if [ -z "$PROBE_ID" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: Probe not found!"
  exit 1
fi
steps.description: Extracts and validates probe ID for use in subsequent queries
steps.expected_result: PROBE_ID variable set with valid probe ID

steps.title: Verify Probe Details
steps.command:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/probes/$PROBE_ID" | jq
steps.description: Retrieves full probe configuration and validates details
steps.expected_result: Probe has correct static_url (cluster API), cluster_id label, management_cluster_id, and private label

steps.title: Login to RHOBS Cell Cluster
steps.command:
export RHOBS_CLUSTER_ID="<rhobs-cell-cluster-id>"
ocm backplane login $RHOBS_CLUSTER_ID
export AGENT_NS=$(oc get deployment -A | grep synthetics-agent | awk '{print $1}')
echo "Agent Namespace: $AGENT_NS"
steps.description: Connects to RHOBS cell cluster where synthetics-agent runs
steps.expected_result: Successfully authenticated, agent namespace identified

steps.title: Check Agent is Running
steps.command:
oc get deployment -n $AGENT_NS rhobs-synthetics-agent
oc logs -n $AGENT_NS deployment/rhobs-synthetics-agent --tail=50
steps.description: Verifies agent deployment is healthy and running
steps.expected_result: Agent deployment shows ready status, logs show recent activity

steps.title: Monitor Agent Polling
steps.command: oc logs -n $AGENT_NS deployment/rhobs-synthetics-agent -f | grep -i "probe\|$CLUSTER_ID"
steps.description: Watches agent logs for evidence of polling API and discovering our probe
steps.expected_result: Logs show 'Fetched N probes from API', 'Found probe for cluster <cluster-id>', 'Creating Probe CR for probe-<id>'

steps.title: Verify Probe CR Created
steps.command:
sleep 60
oc get probes -n $AGENT_NS
oc get probe -n $AGENT_NS | grep $CLUSTER_ID
export PROBE_CR_NAME=$(oc get probe -n $AGENT_NS -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels."rhobs.monitoring/cluster-id" == "'"$CLUSTER_ID"'") | .metadata.name')
echo "Probe CR Name: $PROBE_CR_NAME"
oc get probe -n $AGENT_NS $PROBE_CR_NAME -o yaml
steps.description: Confirms agent created a Probe CR for blackbox-exporter to consume
steps.expected_result: Probe CR exists with correct target URL and labels

steps.title: Check Blackbox Exporter
steps.command:
oc get deployment -n $AGENT_NS | grep blackbox
oc logs -n $AGENT_NS deployment/synthetics-blackbox-prober -f | grep -i "$CLUSTER_API_URL"
steps.description: Verifies blackbox exporter is executing HTTP probes against cluster API
steps.expected_result: Blackbox exporter logs show probe executions against cluster API URL

steps.title: Check Prometheus Scraping Probes
steps.command:
oc get prometheus -n $AGENT_NS
oc exec -n $AGENT_NS prometheus-rhobs-synthetics-0 -- \
  promtool query instant http://localhost:9090 \
  "probe_success{cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"}"
steps.description: Queries Prometheus on RHOBS cell to verify it's scraping probe metrics
steps.expected_result: Returns probe_success metric with value of 1 (success) or 0 (failure)

steps.title: Verify Probe Status Update
steps.command:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/probes/$PROBE_ID" | \
  jq '.status'
steps.description: Checks if agent updated probe status in API based on execution results
steps.expected_result: Status is 'active' (if probe succeeded) or 'failed' (if probe failed), no longer 'pending'

steps.title: Wait for Metrics to Propagate
steps.command:
echo "Waiting 5 minutes for probe metrics to propagate..."
sleep 300
steps.description: Allows time for metrics to be remote-written from RHOBS cell Prometheus to Thanos
steps.expected_result: 5 minute wait completes

steps.title: Query Probe Metrics
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query=probe_success{cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"}" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/api/v1/query" | jq
steps.description: Queries RHOBS/Thanos for probe_success metric
steps.expected_result: Returns probe_success=1 with correct labels (cluster_id, management_cluster_id, probe_type)

steps.title: Query Additional Probe Metrics
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query=probe_duration_seconds{cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"}" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/api/v1/query" | jq

curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query=probe_http_status_code{cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"}" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/api/v1/query" | jq
steps.description: Queries for additional probe metrics like duration and HTTP status code
steps.expected_result: Returns duration metrics and HTTP 200 status code

steps.title: Verify Metric Labels
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "query=probe_success{cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"}" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/api/v1/query" | \
  jq '.data.result[0].metric'
steps.description: Extracts and verifies all required labels are present on probe metrics
steps.expected_result: Labels include cluster_id, management_cluster_id, apiserver_url, probe_type

steps.title: Delete Test Cluster
steps.command:
rosa delete cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME --yes
watch -n 30 rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
steps.description: Deletes the test cluster to validate probe lifecycle cleanup
steps.expected_result: Cluster deletion initiated, status changes to 'uninstalling'

steps.title: Verify HostedCluster Deletion
steps.command: oc get hostedcluster -n $HC_NAMESPACE $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
steps.description: Checks if HostedCluster CR is deleted from MC
steps.expected_result: HostedCluster not found or in 'Deleting' state

steps.title: Verify Probe Deletion from API
steps.command:
sleep 180
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/probes/$PROBE_ID"
steps.description: Waits for RMO to detect cluster deletion and remove probe from API
steps.expected_result: Returns 404 Not Found or similar error

steps.title: Verify Probe CR Deletion from RHOBS Cluster
steps.command: oc get probe -n $AGENT_NS $PROBE_CR_NAME
steps.description: Checks if agent cleaned up Probe CR on RHOBS cell
steps.expected_result: Probe CR not found

success_indicators: Probe registered in RHOBS API with correct details
Probe CR created on RHOBS cell cluster
Probe lifecycle works (deletion cleans up properly)
expected_results.what_success_means: The complete synthetic monitoring system is operational. Clusters are automatically discovered, probes are configured and executed, and results flow to RHOBS where they power availability dashboards and alerts. SREs have visibility into cluster API reachability from external vantage points.
expected_results.what_failure_means: Synthetic monitoring is broken, creating a gap in cluster availability monitoring. SREs may not detect cluster API outages until customers report issues. This defeats the purpose of proactive monitoring and increases MTTR (mean time to resolution) for availability incidents.

failure_scenarios.likely_cause: RMO not watching HostedClusters or API unreachable from MC
debugging_steps: Check RMO watches: oc logs -n $RMO_NS deployment/route-monitor-operator | grep -i watch
Check RMO API client errors: oc logs -n $RMO_NS deployment/route-monitor-operator | grep -i error
Test API connectivity from MC: oc debug node/<node> -- curl -v $RHOBS_API_URL
Verify RMO configuration includes probe-api-url

test_3_synthetic_monitoring.educational_notes: The synthetic monitoring system uses a distributed architecture: route-monitor-operator (RMO) runs on each Management Cluster and watches for HostedCluster CRs. When it detects a new cluster, it registers a probe via the RHOBS synthetics API. The rhobs-synthetics-agent polls the API periodically and creates Probe CRs for the blackbox-exporter to consume. The blackbox-exporter executes HTTP probes against cluster API /readyz endpoints and exposes metrics. Prometheus scrapes these metrics and remote-writes them to RHOBS. This architecture provides external validation of cluster availability independent of the cluster's own monitoring stack.
